clearCameraSettings: Clear saved camera settings from memory
exposureControl: Choose between automatic or manual exposure control
framerateControl: Choose between automatic or manual framerate control
setTargetFps: Set target frames per second (FPS) for camera capture
playbackSpeed: Playback speed (does not affect recording fps)
loadSynchronizedVideosDescription: This page will allow you to load and synchronize pre-recorded videos.
syncInfoTitle: Recording playback may show desynchronization not present in the recorded videos. Matched frame numbers represent images from the same time slice.  We are working on a fix.
syncInfoBody: Browser video playback does not guarantee sample-accurate synchronization across multiple streams. The player uses a leader-follower strategy and corrects drift when it exceeds a small tolerance, but minor desynchronization (1–2 frames) can occur
estimatedFromFrameNumber: Estimated from frame number × recording fps — not read from timestamp data
name: Name
connectCameras: Connect to selected cameras or update connected cameras
showTranslationIndicatorDescription: Display a badge when using AI-generated translations
displayTooltipLong: Display represents the UI rendering performance. It shows how quickly your display receives and renders frames. Performance issues here won't affect recording quality but may impact your ability to monitor cameras in real-time.
statsSourceShort: Display renders frames, Server captures frames.
statsSourceLong: The server is the true rate at which frames are pulled/recorded from the camera, while display is the rate at which they are received and rendered. FreeMoCap prioritizes server-side performance for recording quality, so that number should stay more stable. If the display framerate diverges from the server, it indicates your system resources are taxed. Consider using fewer cameras or decreasing framerate/resolution.
statsCurrentShort: Most recent frame time and corresponding FPS.
statsCurrentLong: This shows the most recent measurement of how long it takes to process a single frame (in milliseconds) and the equivalent frames per second (FPS). Lower frame times and higher FPS indicate better performance.
statsMinShort: Fastest frame time (lowest latency) and highest FPS achieved.
statsMinLong: This represents the minimum time it took to process a single frame during the sampling window. This corresponds to the maximum FPS your system achieved during optimal conditions.
statsMaxShort: Slowest frame time (highest latency) and lowest FPS experienced.
statsMaxLong: This represents the maximum time it took to process a single frame during the sampling window. This corresponds to the minimum FPS your system achieved during worst-case conditions. Occasional spikes are normal, but consistently high values may indicate performance issues.
statsMeanShort: Average frame time and FPS across all samples.
statsMeanLong: The arithmetic mean (average) of all frame times measured during the sampling window and the corresponding FPS. This gives a good overall picture of performance but may be skewed by outliers.
statsMedianShort: Middle value of all frame times (50th percentile).
statsMedianLong: The median represents the middle value when all frame times are sorted from fastest to slowest. Unlike the mean, the median is not affected by extreme outliers, making it a more stable indicator of typical performance.
statsStdDevShort: Measures frame time variability. CV% is relative variability.
statsStdDevLong: Standard deviation measures the amount of variation in frame times. Lower values indicate more consistent performance. The Coefficient of Variation (CV%) expresses this variability as a percentage of the mean, making it easier to compare stability across different frame rates. Lower CV% indicates more stable performance.
pipelineStages_sortHint: Click the column header to sort rows.
pipelineStages_filterCaptureLong: Per-camera work on SkellyCam workers other than skeleton/Charuco tracking and the live preview encode path — for example OpenCV grab()/retrieve() dequeue/decode times — plus multiframe-wide capture metrics like the inter-camera grab spread.
pipelineStages_filterTrackingLong: Skeleton inference: centralized GPU batch (skeleton_inference node), per-camera skeleton_detection, per-camera Charuco board detection when they run on camera workers, and browser-side MediaPipe Tasks pose/hand/face timings when MediaPipe (browser) realtime detection is active.
pipelineStages_filterUiBackendLong: Server-side live preview pipeline: JPEG rotate, resize, and encode plus building the multiplex websocket binary (ws_payload_prepare_ms). Measured on camera processes but dedicated to feeding the UI stream.
pipelineStages_filterUiFrontendLong: Timings measured in the Electron/browser client (JPEG decode, canvas, websocket receive/dispatch, rAF, etc.).
pipelineStages_filterNoneSelected: All categories are unchecked — check one or more to show pipeline rows.
pipelineStages_filterEmptyResult: No rows match the current filters. Enable another category above.
pipelineStages_filterEmptyResultText: No source matches your text filter — clear the search box or try a different term.
pipelineStages_sourceTextFilterPlacehold: Filter sources (e.g. ui, camera:, jpeg, multiframe)
pipelineStages_tableEmptyNoData: No timing samples yet. Ensure timing is enabled and frames are streaming.
pipelineStages_sourceShort: Name of the timed pipeline substage. Click here to restore the default row grouping when a column sort is active.
pipelineStages_sourceLong:
Each row is one instrumented substage. Camera rows are per physical camera in SkellyCam’s camera processes. Skeleton GPU rows come from centralized ONNX inference when enabled. mediapipe_js rows are per camera and per landmarker task (pose, hands, face) from the browser MediaPipe worker when realtime detection uses MediaPipe (browser). Other UI rows are measured on the main thread or decode/canvas workers in the Electron/browser frontend.

Numbers are durations in milliseconds unless the tooltip says otherwise. Samples are collected into a rolling window on the client (up to about one thousand points per row). The server sends timing batches about four times per second; UI metrics are recorded every frame.
pipelineStages_col_recentShort: Most recent value written for this row.
pipelineStages_col_recentLong:
The latest single sample currently stored for this substage after the last backend timing batch or UI measurement. For server-driven rows, this is typically the last value from the most recent ~250 ms batch. For UI rows, it is the last frame’s measurement.

The secondary line shows an instantaneous “fps” computed as 1000 / duration_ms for that one sample (only meaningful when the quantity is actually a time duration).
pipelineStages_col_meanShort: Average of all samples in the rolling window.
pipelineStages_col_meanLong:
Arithmetic mean of every duration sample retained for this row in the client-side window. Useful for spotting which substages dominate overall time on average.

The secondary line is 1000 / mean_ms, treating the mean as if it were a frame period. That fps analog is helpful for comparing rows but is not the same as end-to-end camera FPS.
pipelineStages_col_medianLong:
Half of the samples in the window are faster than the median and half are slower. Unlike the mean, the median is resistant to occasional huge spikes, so it often reflects “typical” latency for this substage.

Secondary line: fps analog from 1000 / median_ms.
pipelineStages_col_stdDevShort: Standard deviation (ms) and coefficient of variation (%).
pipelineStages_col_stdDevLong:
Standard deviation quantifies how spread out durations are: higher means jitterier performance for this substage. CV% (coefficient of variation) is standard deviation divided by the mean, expressed as a percentage—handy for comparing relative variability even when mean latencies differ.

Large CV% on a cheap stage can still be harmless; on a hot path it often means inconsistent load or contention.
pipelineStages_col_maxShort: Slowest sample observed in the window (worst-case latency).
pipelineStages_col_maxLong:
Maximum duration recorded for this substage during the window—the tail latency advertisers care about. Occasional spikes are normal (GC, OS scheduling); sustained high max values usually merit investigation.

Secondary line: fps analog from the slowest sample (1000 / max_ms), i.e. the lowest instantaneous “fps” implied by that worst spike.
pipelineStages_col_minShort: Fastest sample observed in the window (best-case latency).
pipelineStages_col_minLong:
Minimum duration in the window—the best observed case. Helps bound how fast the stage can run under ideal conditions.

Secondary line: fps analog from the fastest sample (1000 / min_ms).
pipelineStages_row_unknownShort: Pipeline timing sample for this substage.
pipelineStages_row_unknownLong: Duration or metric samples for this instrumented key (shown as the raw row id in developer contexts). Enable pipeline timing on the server and refer to FreeMoCap/SkellyCam source for the exact timer boundaries.
pipelineStages_row_skel_frame_readShort: GPU node: assemble frames for inference.
pipelineStages_row_skel_frame_readLong:
Time for the centralized skeleton inference worker to read or prepare multi-camera image data before running the neural network.

Relevant only when centralized GPU inference is enabled.
pipelineStages_row_skel_predict_batchSho: GPU node: single batched ONNX inference.
pipelineStages_row_skel_predict_batchLon:
Duration of the batched neural-network prediction over all cameras sharing one GPU submit.

Dominates GPU-mode skeleton latency when batch sizes are large.
pipelineStages_row_skel_dropped_framesSh: Frames skipped in GPU skeleton path (count).
pipelineStages_row_skel_dropped_framesLo:
Reported value is a count of dropped frames in the inference batching window, not a duration in milliseconds despite the table’s generic “ms” formatting.

Non-zero values mean the GPU worker could not keep up with the realtime stream.
pipelineStages_row_mpjs_pose_detect_msLo:
Wall time for PoseLandmarker.detectForVideo on this camera's frame in the dedicated MediaPipe worker during one realtime batch.

Shown when the realtime detector is MediaPipe (browser). There is one row per camera for pose, hands, and face.
pipelineStages_row_mpjs_hand_detect_msLo:
Wall time for HandLandmarker.detectForVideo on this camera's frame (same batch as pose/face).

Includes both hands when detected; one landmarker invocation per camera per frame.
pipelineStages_row_mpjs_face_detect_msLo:
Wall time for FaceLandmarker.detectForVideo on this camera's frame in the MediaPipe worker.

Uses the contour subset mapped into the holistic keypoint buffer sent to the server.
pipelineStages_row_cam_jpeg_encode_msSho: JPEG compression for the live preview stream.
pipelineStages_row_cam_jpeg_encode_msLon:
Server-side time spent in cv2.imencode while building the compressed image forwarded to the UI over the websocket.

Impacts preview quality versus bandwidth; independent of motion-capture accuracy.
pipelineStages_row_cam_jpeg_resize_msLon:
Server-side time in cv2.resize when downsampling or fitting the camera frame to the websocket preview dimensions.

Runs once per camera per preview frame; separate from skeleton / recording pipelines.
pipelineStages_row_cam_jpeg_rotate_msLon:
Server-side time in cv2.rotate when the camera is configured with a non-default orientation for the live preview.

Absent or zero when rotation is disabled.
pipelineStages_row_cam_ws_payload_prepar: Build multiplex websocket preview binary on the server.

Wall-clock time inside create_frontend_payload: allocating/copying the payload buffer, writing header and footer, and for every camera in the group running rotate (if any), resize, JPEG encode, and copying JPEG bytes into the multiplex blob.

The same total milliseconds is recorded once per camera row so it appears next to per-camera jpeg_* stages; it is one shared multiplex build, not per-camera wall time.
pipelineStages_row_mf_inter_camera_grab_:
For each multiframe sent to the UI, max(post_frame_grab_ns) − min(post_frame_grab_ns) across cameras — the wall time between the earliest and latest grab() return. A measure of inter-camera grab synchronization.

Low values mean cameras returned grabs nearly simultaneously; high values mean some cameras lag others.

Mirrors the post-recording inter-camera grab sync stat but measured live, one sample per built websocket payload.
pipelineStages_row_cam_grab_request_to_s:
Time inside VideoCapture.grab() for this camera — from just before dequeue until the driver returns. Recorded live every captured frame while the camera is open.

Mirrors recording post-process stats (grab request → grab success).
pipelineStages_row_cam_retrieve_request_:
Time inside VideoCapture.retrieve() to decode the grabbed frame into the pixel buffer (e.g. MJPEG → BGR). Recorded live every captured frame.

Mirrors recording post-process stats (retrieve request → retrieve success).
pipelineStages_row_cam_cap_prop_pos_minu: Camera clock vs. host perf_counter offset (ms).

cv2.VideoCapture.get(cv2.CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC) sampled immediately after cap.grab() minus the host time.perf_counter() captured just before the grab call (converted to ms).

Both clocks have arbitrary origins, so the absolute value is not physically meaningful — but its drift across frames (mean trend), jitter (stdDev / CV%), and tail spikes (max) reveal skew between the camera/driver clock and the host's perf_counter. Stable on healthy cameras; growing means the camera clock is running faster or slower than the host; large spikes hint at driver buffering delays.

Not all OpenCV backends populate CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC for live cameras; absent samples mean the backend returned 0.
pipelineStages_row_cam_skeleton_detectio:
Time for the camera worker’s skeleton detector (e.g. MediaPipe/tracker backend) on one frame.

In centralized GPU mode this row may be absent or minimal because inference moves to the skeleton_inference node.
pipelineStages_row_cam_charuco_detection:
Time spent locating the calibration board and extracting corners on this camera stream.

Spikes often correlate with motion blur or poor lighting.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_ack_to_receiv: After frame ACK until full JPEG payload bytes arrive.

Window performance time from when the client sends websocket frameAcknowledgment for the previous multiplexed preview frame until the browser finishes receiving the next binary JPEG payload (ArrayBuffer in onmessage).

Measures server encode/pipeline plus network delivery for the following frame; not JPEG decode. No sample on the very first preview frame (nothing was ACK’d yet). All cameras in the bundle share the same measured RTT.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_ws_binary_int: Time since previous multiplex JPEG arrived on the WebSocket.

Difference between performance.now() when two successive multiplex preview binaries are delivered (same WebSocket, excluding keypoints frames).

Browsers expose a WebSocket message only after the full frame is assembled, so this is not wire-level throughput—but when only one preview is in flight it tracks how often complete payloads reach JS (server + network + TCP pacing). First frame after connect has no interval sample.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_ws_dispatch_l: Browser timestamp vs. handler start for each WS binary.

performance.now() minus MessageEvent.timeStamp when the multiplex JPEG ArrayBuffer is handled.

Mostly main-thread scheduling delay between the engine finishing the WebSocket message and your callback running; typically sub-millisecond unless the tab is busy.
pipelineStages_row_ui_raf_to_rendered_ms: Main-thread rAF body start → render ack.

Elapsed window performance time from the start of the requestAnimationFrame callback body that removed this JPEG from the pending queue and started decode, until the main thread handles renderAck after transferFromImageBitmap in the offscreen worker.

Includes JPEG/ImageBitmap decode, optional overlay compositing, posting to the canvas worker, worker rAF scheduling, and GPU presentation—everything after queuing but excluding idle wait before that rAF tick runs and excluding ACK→JPEG-received network time.

Use the sibling UI rows (JPEG decode worker, bridge, canvas worker rAF wait, bitmap transfer) to see which slice dominates.
pipelineStages_row_ui_raf_body_before_de: Same rAF tick: ack / JSON / keypoints before decode starts.

Window time from the start of this tick’s requestAnimationFrame callback body (same origin as “rAF tick → rendered”) until the main thread posts the multiplex JPEG to the decode worker.

Captures frameAcknowledgment send, buffered frontend_json / binary keypoints dispatch, and any synchronous work scheduled before decode is queued—not JPEG decode itself.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_decode_worker:
Wall time inside the dedicated decode worker from receiving the ArrayBuffer until all cameras in the bundle finish sequential createImageBitmap.

Uses the worker’s performance clock (aligned with the window in dedicated workers). Excludes structured-clone and main-thread continuation overhead, which show up in “JPEG decode bridge”.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_decode_main_w: Main thread: post decode → dispatchFrames entry.

Window performance time from when the main thread transfers the multiplex payload to the decode worker until dispatchFrames begins for this result—i.e. the full round-trip including worker work, transfer back of ImageBitmap handles, and microtask scheduling.

Approximately equals decode worker ms + decode bridge ms for that frame.
pipelineStages_row_ui_jpeg_decode_bridge: IPC + scheduling: main wait minus worker wall time.

max(0, JPEG decode total wait − JPEG decode worker ms).

Absorbs structured clone / transfer overhead, message queues, and delay until the Promise continuation runs on the main thread. Large spikes often mean the main thread was busy.
pipelineStages_row_ui_main_dispatch_to_c: Window time from entering dispatchFrames until this camera’s bitmap is posted to its offscreen canvas worker, including synchronous setup. When overlays are composited asynchronously, this ends when the overlay Promise resolves just before the post—so it includes overlay GPU time for that path.
pipelineStages_row_ui_canvas_worker_rece:
performance.now() in the canvas worker when the frame message is handled, minus mainSentAtMs captured immediately before postMessage on the window thread.

Mostly cross-thread delivery and worker event-loop latency; should usually be sub‑millisecond.
pipelineStages_row_ui_canvas_worker_raf_: Canvas worker: frame received → rAF callback start.

Time from when the offscreen worker’s onmessage stores the ImageBitmap until the requestAnimationFrame callback that calls transferFromImageBitmap begins.

Typical source of multi‑ms latency when preview targets vsync: one worker animation frame of wait.
pipelineStages_row_ui_canvas_bitmap_tran:
Measured in the offscreen worker around transferFromImageBitmap (same interval previously surfaced as a mis-labeled “overlay render” row).

Mostly GPU/compositor work for that blit; uses the worker clock for duration.
pipelineStages_row_ui_render_ack_deliver:
Window performance.now() when the renderAck notification is handled minus MessageEvent.timeStamp for that same event—both on the main thread/realm, so this avoids bogus multi‑second values from subtracting a dedicated worker’s performance.now() when its time origin does not match the window (seen in some Electron/embed builds).

Measures how long after the browser queued the worker message your onmessage handler ran; typically sub‑millisecond unless the main thread is busy.
